text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
InCompany(x) ::: x is in the company building.
Lunchtime(x) ::: x has lunch.
AtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorksRemotely(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InOtherCountries(x) ::: x works in other countries.
James ::: James (specific individual)
Premises:
∀x (Employee(x) ∧ SchedulesMeeting(x, y) → InCompany(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will go to the company building today.
∀x (Lunchtime(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company building schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Lunchtime(x) → (InCompany(x) ∨ AtHome(x))) ::: Employees have lunch either in the company building or at home.
∀x (AtHome(x) → WorksRemotely(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, they are working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountries(x) → WorksRemotely(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
¬Manager(x) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
Question:
James is a manager if and only if he will appear in the company today.
